paper text.text: It remains to exclude $n_e=3$. In this case the applicable row gives a single nonplanar completion $B+E'$. It has no $K_5$ minor, since contracting $bd$ into $d$ in the minor of Lemma~\ref{r1:triangle-minor} with $U=B\cup bd$ gives $B+ac+ad+ae+cd+de$. The same row applies after any allowed reduction of $B$, so the resulting graph is nontoroidal whenever its completion is nonplanar. Corollary~\ref{common:reduced-forms} therefore applies with added edges $E'$. This gives $9{,}127$ candidates without $cd$ and $8{,}967$ with $cd$. In each, deleting or contracting one edge gives a nontoroidal minor~\supp{E24}. Thus $n_e=2$, and the first two rows give the claimed form of $G$ and the two nonplanar completions in~\eqref{r1:c1-caps}.
